title: Structs with Functions
learningObjectives: Pass struct objects by value or reference appropriately.
Use const references for read-only structured input.
Return small structured results by value.
Mutate caller-owned objects through references intentionally.

understand.concept: Struct objects can be passed by value, reference or const reference to functions. Returning a struct by value is a convenient way to produce a result.
understand.whyItMatters: Functions can operate on structured data without scattered parameters.
understand.explain: Prefer const reference for read-only larger objects and return by value when creating a result.

examples.title: Pass const reference
examples.code: struct Point{int x;int y;};\nint sum(const Point& p){return p.x+p.y;}
examples.explanation: The function reads fields without copying the object.

examples.title: Return struct
examples.explanation: Returning a small aggregate by value is convenient.

examples.title: Modify reference
examples.code: struct Score{int value;};\nvoid add(Score& s,int n){s.value+=n;}
examples.explanation: Reference parameter changes the caller's object.

examples.title: Multiple structured parameters
examples.code: struct Point{int x;int y;};\nint distanceSquared(Point a,Point b){int dx=a.x-b.x,dy=a.y-b.y;return dx*dx+dy*dy;}
examples.explanation: The function accepts two structured values.

practise.guidedTask: For Structs with Functions, trace every example. List each type, object, member, initial value, access path, and state change. Identify where encapsulation or initialization affects correctness.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ model focused on Structs with Functions (such as a Point, Student, Product, or Account). Include multiple objects, initialization, at least one operation/member access, and test normal, boundary and invalid states. Explain which fields should be public or private and why.
hints: Define the type and its responsibilities before creating objects.
Initialize members deliberately and trace their values.
Use dot for objects and arrow only for pointers.
Keep fields private when they must enforce rules.
Test object creation, valid operations and rejected updates.

questions.explanation: const reference avoids copy and mutation.

options: Convenient and safe for value results
questions.answer: Convenient and safe for value results
questions.explanation: Return by value is a normal C++ pattern.
A non-const reference aliases the caller object.
Passing by value copies or moves the object.
Related values can be represented as one object.
